summary:
The Mars Exploration Mission project consists of developing an interactive simulator that recreates the challenges astronauts may face during a mission to Mars. The main objective is to demonstrate how decision-making affects crew safety, resource management and mission success.

The simulator includes different scenarios involving energy production, oxygen supply, food and water management, astronaut health, space agriculture, equipment maintenance and radiation exposure.

Throughout the mission, players must make decisions, such as protecting solar panels during storms, maintaining exercise routines, repairing essential systems or prioritising safety during emergencies. Each choice has consequences that can affect available resources and the crew's performance.

The project combines smaller technical tasks with more complex missions, encouraging players to balance scientific objectives with survival requirements.

Ultimately, the simulator highlights the importance of planning, adaptability and responsible resource management in space exploration, showing that successful missions depend on both advanced technology and effective human decision-making.
details:
Our project consists of creating an interactive survival game based on a mission to Mars, using scientific information and research from NASA and other reliable sources. The main idea is to simulate the difficulties that astronauts could face when living on Mars, such as the lack of water, food, oxygen and energy, as well as the dangers of solar radiation and the effects of reduced gravity on the human body.

The game works through a series of daily missions and special missions that alternate throughout the game. During daily missions, players must make basic decisions to maintain their survival, such as drinking water, eating food or harvesting crops. Special missions introduce more complicated situations, such as problems with solar panels, oxygen production, muscle loss or solar storms. On days when a special mission takes place, there is no daily mission. Players must choose between different options, and each decision can have consequences for their resources and their chances of survival.

To develop the game, we used Python and HTML as programming languages. Python is used to create the main game logic, including the functions, questions, options and consequences of the players' decisions. HTML is used to work on the web-based presentation and structure of the game. We asked ChatGPT to help us with the creation of the html to make more visual the decisions the player is choosing.  We organised the missions into different functions so that each challenge could work independently and be included in the correct order. We also used scientific information to make the situations and decisions as realistic and educational as possible.

One of the main benefits of our programme is that it combines learning and entertainment. Players can discover scientific facts about Mars while improving their problem-solving, decision-making and critical-thinking skills. It also helps them understand how important it is to manage limited resources and how difficult it would be to survive in an environment so different from Earth.

Our main objective when developing this programme was to create an educational and interactive experience that would make learning about space exploration more interesting. We wanted players to understand the challenges of a possible human mission to Mars, learn about the importance of scientific research and realise how every decision can affect survival. We also aimed to develop our programming skills, learn how to organise code into functions and use technology to transform scientific information into an interactive game.
